newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest hydropower dam operations normal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest hydropower dam operations normal.

text.p: Federal dams in the U.S. Northwest are largely operating at normal rates for this time of year, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, which operates most of the projects, said Tuesday.
"There is nothing unusual for fall operation," said Cindy Hendrickson, chief of the agency's reservoir control center in Portland, Ore.
Although rainfall in the Columbia River basin was about 131 percent of normal in October, "rain has not been significant or concentrated enough (to affect dam operations)," she said.
The Corps is working now to restore reservoirs back to flood control levels by the end of the year, Hendrickson noted.
"(But) we can't reduce the (out)flows anymore so we have to wait for mother nature," she explained.
Flows from most dams are at minimum levels necessary for system support, and inflows are largely level with outflows, she added.
The Dworshak project in Idaho, for instance, stands at 1,520 feet, compared with a year-end target of 1,558 feet, Hendrickson said.

The reservoir was brought down to the 1,520-foot level for flow augmentation related to fish migration in August and September, but precipitation has not been high enough to boost it back up, she said.
